significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that a capability emerges when task-relevant residual-stream features become disentangled and that the measurable separability transition predicts the behavioral jump "better and more smoothly than the loss curve," supplemented by the form-(ii) claim that ablating those features selectively removes the skill. This establishes both a cross-checkpoint behavioral phenomenon and a causal mechanism, constraining when capabilities should appear, which internal change explains their appearance, and whether loss alone is an adequate progress measure. Wei et al. (2022) and Schaeffer et al. (NeurIPS 2023) frame emergence respectively as a scaling phenomenon and as potentially induced by discontinuous metrics, while Nanda et al. (ICLR 2023) shows that internal progress measures can explain a phase transition; a negative result here would therefore reject feature disentanglement as a general account of emergence, although it would not by itself settle every metric-artifact explanation. Verified-true and verified-false are distinguishable despite some latitude among the proposed geometry metrics, and the topic-substitution check lowers no score: merely restating the language–intelligence topic would omit the specific predictive geometry law and causal feature account that support an above-median rating.

reach.justification: The named handle is the checkpoint-level "feature separability" transition, proposed as an "early-warning signal for capability onset," together with selective ablation of the newly disentangled features as an intervention. It is potentially ex ante when separability "precedes" the behavioral jump, leaving an action window for capability monitoring, but the alternative wording "or coincides" means the claim does not guarantee lead time in every case. After per-model feature re-extraction, the substantive conclusion would still predict an ordering and coupling—separability should rise before or with behavioral emergence and outperform loss as a predictor—rather than merely providing a procedure for searching for arbitrary directions; the asserted scope covers multiple capabilities and training trajectories, with model developers and capability auditors as plausible downstream users. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score because the broad language–intelligence topic alone supplies neither this transferable predictor nor an auditing handle, though the lack of a guaranteed pre-outcome signal and uncertain extension beyond language-model capabilities keep the reach below 9.
